_source: Received-Masoretic extraordinary points (puncta extraordinaria) where the received tradition differs from the dots the WLC (Leningrad Codex) carries. The dotted letters are as enumerated in Avot de-Rabbi Natan (A) 34 (the ten Torah passages) and in A.E. Brouwer, 'Typographic details in the Hebrew Bible' (all fifteen passages). 'add' = a dot the received tradition counts that the WLC lacks (tradition 'masoretic-received'). 'not-received' = a WLC dot the received tradition does not count; it stays tagged 'leningrad' and gains received:false.

sources.BROUWER: A.E. Brouwer, "Typographic details in the Hebrew Bible" (https://aeb.win.tue.nl/natlang/hebrew/hebrew_bible.html)

entries.note: ARN 34: dotted on א, י, ו of אליו. Brouwer: 3 dots on איו; BHS also dots the ל.
The WLC encodes U+05C4 after the ק, before the shureq vav.
ARN 34: dotted on the vav of the first ובקומה. Brouwer: 1 dot on ו.
The WLC encodes U+05C4 after the ר, before the holam vav.
ARN 34: dotted on the vav of עשרון. Brouwer: 1 dot on ו.
ARN 34: dotted on לנו ולבנינו and on the ע of עד (11 dots). Brouwer: 11 dots; BHS does not dot the ע.
